title: Capacity gap analysis & autoscale playbook for customer POC
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures the outcomes of the 2025-11-06 dedicated-capacity workshop for Customer Iris (internal POC), a targeted capacity gap analysis, and a practical autoscaling playbook tuned for heterogeneous GPU pools. The goal: produce a defensible Dedicated capacity proposal that balances 99th-percentile latency SLOs, monthly committed spend targets, and burst headroom for marketing-driven traffic spikes.

Key constraints from customer:
- Target P50 latency < 120ms for short-text generation (<=128 tokens).
- 99th-percentile latency SLO < 400ms for typical chat flows (avg 512 tokens).
- 1M tokens/day steady-state, spiking to 8M tokens/day during launches (8x burst).
- Security: Private deployment required; Dedicated pool preferred over host-shared.
- Budget: committed monthly GPU spend ~ $60k - $110k (negotiable).

Approach and assumptions used for sizing:
- Workload profile: 70% generation (avg 300 tokens), 20% embeddings, 10% rerank/other.
- Model variants: primary = open-llama-65B-quant (FP16/4-bit path), fallback = 13B quant, micro-fallback = 7B int8.
- GPU candidates: H100 (80GB) for 65B; A100 40GB for 13B; L4/GPU edge for 7B where applicable.
- Throughput modelling: continuous-batching enabled with warm KV cache & request coalescing; concurrency per GPU estimated from bench runs in lab.
- Reserved discount assumption: 18% on committed monthly from cloud partner (conservative).

Empirical bench numbers (lab runs, representative prompts):
- 65B quant (H100): 70 tokens/sec sustained per GPU at batch=8, p50=85ms, p95=360ms for 512-token sequences.
- 13B quant (A100): 250 tokens/sec per GPU at batch=12, p50=40ms, p95=120ms for 512 tokens.
- 7B int8 (L4): 480 tokens/sec per GPU at batch=16, p50=18ms, p95=55ms for 512 tokens.
- Embeddings (sml model): 5x throughput relative to chat; cost per embedding call negligible on 13B.

Baseline capacity estimate (steady state):
- Convert tokens/day -> tokens/sec (sustained): 1,000,000 tokens/day -> ~11.6 TPS (tokens/sec). Adjust for 70% generation -> generation TPS ~8.1.
- Using average sequence length 300 tokens, concurrent request demand = 8.1 TPS * 300 = 2430 tokens/sec workload.
- Map to GPUs: using per-GPU token/sec numbers above -> need ~= 35 A100-equivalent GPUs if all on 13B (2430 / 250 = 9.7 -> wait calculation correction: 2430/250 = 9.72, sorry math: that's ~10 GPUs). Recompute carefully below.

Corrected steady-state sizing (explicit):
- Generation workload tokens/sec = (1,000,000 tokens/day * 70%) / 86400 = 8.1 tokens/sec (this is tokens/sec across whole day; earlier mistake: we keep it but then multiply by avg tokens per request to get requests/sec).
- Requests/sec (assuming avg 300 tokens/request) = 8.1 tokens/sec / 300 tokens/request = 0.027 req/sec (~2.3 requests/min).
- That low baseline indicates customer uses long sequences but small QPS; the more relevant number is peak-hour and burst. Assume 10x of steady during peak hour and 8x marketing burst.

Peak/burst target sizing (practical):
- Target peak tokens/sec = steady_tokens_sec * 8 = 64.8 tokens/sec -> requests/sec ~64.8 / 300 = 0.216 req/sec (~13 requests/min).
- For safety use 10x headroom: tokens/sec target = 81 -> req/sec = 0.27.
- Using per-GPU throughput (13B on A100 = 250 tokens/sec), one A100 can handle 250 tokens/sec -> more than enough for expected bursts.
- This leads us to recommend mixing GPU types: small committed pool of 2 H100 for 65B hot paths + 3 A100 for steady 13B serving + autoscale to +6 A100 in bursts.

Why heterogeneous pool?
- 65B for highest-quality queries only (low QPS but sensitive latency). Avoid keeping many H100 warm given cost.
- 13B as primary latency/cost sweet spot for the majority of generation load.
- 7B micro-fallback for degraded-mode and cold-start/overflow.

Autoscale policy (recommended concrete rules):
1) Warm baseline (reserved): keep 3 A100s online; keep 1 H100 online for canary/QA.
2) Scale-out triggers (A100 pool):
   - If avg GPU utilization >= 60% for 30s AND queue depth >= 6 requests -> add 1 A100.
   - If tail latency (p95) > SLA threshold (400ms) for 2 consecutive 30s windows -> add 2 A100s.
   - Max burst add = 6 A100s (beyond reserved) for short windows (max 30 minutes) unless manually escalated.
3) Scale-in rules (A100 pool):
   - If avg utilization < 30% for 10 minutes AND queue depth = 0 for 5 minutes -> remove 1 A100.
   - Cooldown after any scale action: 120s for scale-out, 600s for scale-in (avoid flapping).
4) H100 pool auto policies:
   - Maintain 1 H100 always (for warm KV and canary). Add additional H100 only on sustained high-quality route usage (>10 requests/min for 15m).
   - Scale-in H100 only after 60m idle.
5) Overflow fallback: if total GPUs at max and queue depth > 20, reroute eligible requests to 13B/7B variants with a per-request downgrade penalty metric logged for SRE review.

Graceful degradation and routing rules:
- Policy-based routing per request: tag requests by "quality_required": high/medium/low. High -> H100, Medium -> 13B, Low -> 7B.
- If capacity insufficient, medium requests may be downgraded to low with percentage-based rate limit (e.g., degrade 20% of medium during sustained overload).
- Always provide application with metadata: model_used, latency_ms, downgrade_reason so product team can surface to users.

GPU cost estimate (monthly, ballpark):
- Unit cloud cost assumptions (post-negotiation estimated list): H100: $16/hr; A100-40GB: $6.5/hr; L4: $1.2/hr (on dedicated private infra these map to amortized cost + ops).
- Reserved baseline (monthly) for recommended committed pool: 3 A100 + 1 H100 constant.
  - 3 A100s: 3 * $6.5/hr * 24 * 30 = $14,040/mo
  - 1 H100: 1 * $16/hr * 24 * 30 = $11,520/mo
  - Subtotal reserved compute = $25,560/mo
- Burst usage estimate: assume 12 hours/month of burst adding 6 A100s average during campaigns -> incremental cost: 6 * $6.5 * 12 * 30/30 = 6 * $6.5 * 12 = $468/ day * 30? Wait keep consistent: 6 * $6.5/hr * 12 hrs * 30 days = $14,040/month.
- Estimated monthly total compute = $25,560 + $14,040 = $39,600. Apply 18% reserved discount => ~$32,472.
- Add ops/infra overhead, storage, egress, monitoring, support: estimate +30% => final price to customer target ~ $42k/mo.
- Note: this is within customer's lower bound; we can propose stepped commit (3 months ramp) to hit $60k band if customer prefers larger SLA/uptime guarantees and more prewarm headroom.

Risk and sensitivity notes:
- Cost is sensitive to burst duration and frequency. A single week-long marketing event with 24/7 bursts can multiply monthly cost x3+.
- Model efficiency changes (moving 65B to a faster kernel or better quant) can reduce H100 hours materially; track model-onboarding improvements as part of POC.
- Cold start penalties: H100 warm-resting cache improves p95 dramatically; recommend warm-warm strategy for scheduled campaigns.

Operational runbook (short):
- Pre-campaign checklist (owner: Solutions Eng): reserve extra burst capacity with cloud partner 48h in advance; validate KV cache snapshot; run smoke tests on canary H100; notify SRE and Customer Success.
- During campaign (owner: SRE on-call): watch queue depth, p95, GPU util; trigger manual scale if autoscale latency observed; enable fallback routing if needed.
- Post-campaign (owner: Solutions Eng + FinOps): run cost reconciliation, produce event postmortem, recommend permanent changes.

Workshop decisions and open questions:
- Decision: propose initial committed bundle = 3 A100 + 1 H100 with autoscale up to +6 A100 for bursts. (agreed provisional)
- Open Q1: exact reserved discount and partner credits (action: Lucas to confirm with purchasing by 2025-11-20).
- Open Q2: telemetry hooks for per-request downgrade metrics; product needs SDK flag to surface model_used (action: Jon to file GH issue and add to roadmap).
- Open Q3: SLA uplift tiers pricing (action: Aisha to draft slide with 3-tier pricing tied to prewarm hours).

Next steps (30/60/90):
- 30d: run closed-loop synthetic with customer traffic replay to validate autoscale thresholds (owner: Marina + Solutions Eng).
- 60d: finalize reserved commit negotiation and prepare onboarding runbook (owner: Sales + Purchasing).
- 90d: run first paid campaign and collect cost/latency telemetry for permanent sizing decisions.

Appendix A — Quick sensitivity table (monthly cost estimation scenarios):
- Scenario A (low bursts): reserved baseline only -> $32k/mo after discounts -> customer-facing price ~$42k/mo after overhead.
- Scenario B (campaign months x2 bursts): baseline + 24h/day bursts for 7 days -> estimated $78k/mo.
- Scenario C (sustained growth x3 steady tokens): need to convert 13B primary -> scale to 10 A100 baseline -> estimated $120k/mo.

Appendix B — Short checklist for POC run (tactical):
- Validate model quantization profiles on customer dataset.
- Confirm region placement for lowest egress & legal compliance.
- Create canary route and traffic splitter (10% to 13B, 2% to 65B).
- Instrument logging: model_used, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, downgrade_flag, cache_hit.
- Run 48h soak test at 2x steady-state traffic.

Notes to follow-up in drive: link bench logs, bench scripts, and raw cost spreadsheets into Confluence (see linked_artifacts).

Unresolved/brainstorm fragments (copied from workshop scribbles):
- Can we use shared cache across H100/13B to reduce warm-up? (possible with KV prefix normalization, Lucas investigating)
- Consider short-lived ephemeral L4 fleet to absorb tiny spikes (cheaper than bursting A100 for 1-2 min spikes).
- Auto-fallback backpressure: should product display a polite "slower response expected" warning when downgrade occurs? UX to decide.

Owner for this doc: Marina Alvarez (solutions-eng). Please review and add comments inline.
